## Takeaways

_(This prose is preserved across `run_eval.py` runs — the script only rewrites
the table block above. Update numbers here by reading the table.)_

- Gold labels are **human-made, independent** of the extractor (`claude-haiku-5-5`),
  so the comparison is not circular.
- The 32-trial gold set is small (~100 positives); low-support categories
  (smoking, bmi, diabetes have 1–2 each) have unstable per-category scores — read
  the bootstrap CI on overall F1, not the tiny-category cells.
- **2 of the 32 gold trials were picked specifically to cover `bmi`** (not random);
  the rest are a random mix of phases/sponsors/cancer types.
- Only category **presence** is scored. `threshold`, `absolute`, and `section` are
  shown in the app but not graded here.

### Methodology notes
- The extractor prompt was tuned partly by inspecting these gold trials, so the
  score reflects some fitting to this set. After the v2 full re-extraction, the
  score reflects the same prompt applied uniformly to all 1011 trials.
- Deterministic guards in `logic.py` (`drop_noise`) remove known model errors
  before scoring and before the app sees them: bare adult-age floors, child-
  exclusion boilerplate, and quotes that lack their category's keyword
  (e.g. an `hiv` row quoting only hepatitis B/C).

### How to reproduce
```bash
python eval/run_eval.py   # reads exclusions.csv + gold_labels.csv, rewrites the table block only
```
